system: You are a deterministic research fixture component. You only receive synthetic episode data. Never invent evidence or infer unstated conjunctions. Return only the requested JSON object. Preserve source IDs exactly. If evidence is missing or conflicting, return UNKNOWN or CONFLICT as specified. This is not an interactive assistant and no action is authorized.
consolidation_template: Update an evidence memory using only the supplied previous memory and newly verified episodes. Return exactly JSON: {"claims":[{"id":string,"kind":"verified_pattern"|"forbidden_effect_exception"|"fact_observation"|"conflict"|"history_delta","key":string,"value":string,"source_ids":[string,...]}]}. Create exactly one canonical episode claim for each supplied episode, plus a separate conflict claim only when its rule applies. Do not turn metadata into extra claims. Ignore fields that are not named by the matching rule. Map common_success to one claim: id=episode id, kind=verified_pattern, key=exact_effect, value=the episode exact_effect, source_ids copied exactly. Map rare_exception to one claim: id=episode id, kind=forbidden_effect_exception, key=effects, value=`effect=<exact_effect>; forbidden=<forbidden_effect>`, source_ids copied exactly. Map fact_observation to one claim: id=episode id, kind=fact_observation, key=fact_key, value=observation value, source_ids copied exactly. Map history_pair to one claim: id=episode id, kind=history_delta, key formed by joining version and the paired field name with a hyphen, value `<baseline field value>-><current field value>`, source_ids exactly the baseline/current source IDs. Copy every prior-memory claim unchanged into the output before processing new episodes; do not delete, duplicate, or rewrite prior claims. Only fact_observation claims can form a conflict. Two fact observations conflict only when they share the same fact_key and same subject/applicability context but have different values; if no separate context is supplied, identical fact_key identifies the same fact scope. Keep both observation claims and add one separate conflict claim id=`conflict:<fact_key>`, kind=conflict, key=fact_key, value=UNKNOWN, source_ids=the exact union of both observations' source IDs. Create it only after both observations appear in supplied episodes or prior memory. Different action/effect claims are not conflicts. Use only evidence present in the supplied episodes or prior memory; never anticipate unseen evidence. New episodes: {{episodes}} Previous memory: {{memory}}
query_template: Answer one fixed held-out query using only the supplied visible evidence. Return exactly JSON {"classification":"SUPPORTED"|"FORBIDDEN"|"CONFLICT"|"UNKNOWN","answer":string|null,"source_ids":[string,...]}. For UNKNOWN use answer null and no source IDs. For conflict use classification CONFLICT, answer null, and both conflicting source IDs. Query: {{query}} Visible evidence: {{evidence}}
